# Markdown and Input Safety Requirements Quality Checklist: Projects — creation, record, membership and lifecycle

**Purpose**: Validate that the description grammar, link-scheme allowlist, escaping and storage requirements are defined precisely enough to implement, and precisely enough to refuse everything outside the subset
**Created**: 2026-08-31
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Grammar Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Is the treatment of plain paragraphs, blank lines and single newlines specified, given none of them appears in FR-010's enumerated subset yet every description needs them? [Gap, Completeness, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK002 Are the accepted syntax spellings specified for bold and italic — asterisks, underscores, or both? [Gap, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK003 Are the permitted heading levels specified, and how they relate to the heading structure of the screen that already surrounds the description? [Gap, Accessibility, Spec §FR-010, §FR-039]
- [x] CHK004 Is it specified whether lists may nest, and to what depth? [Gap, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK005 Are nesting rules specified for inline constructs — whether a link may contain bold, whether inline code may contain a link, and which construct wins when they overlap? [Gap, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK006 Is the numbered list's numbering behaviour specified — whether the source ordinals are honoured or renumbered? [Gap, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK007 Is backslash-escape behaviour specified, so a user can write a literal asterisk? [Gap, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK008 Is the parser required to be total — to produce output for every possible input rather than failing on malformed source? [Gap, Exception Flow, Spec §FR-010, §FR-039]

## Constructs Outside the Subset

- [x] CHK009 Is "renders as its own literal text" stated as the rule for every construct outside the subset, or only for the three the Edge Cases name? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK010 Is the treatment specified for fenced code blocks, blockquotes and horizontal rules, none of which is named as either supported or excluded? [Gap, Completeness, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK011 Is the treatment specified for autolinks, reference-style links and bare URLs, given FR-011 governs only a link's scheme? [Gap, Spec §FR-010, §FR-011]
- [x] CHK012 Is it stated whether an unsupported construct renders as its literal source characters or as the text it would have produced? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-010, §Edge Cases]

## Link Safety

- [x] CHK013 Is scheme matching specified as case-insensitive, so a mixed-case scheme cannot evade the allowlist? [Gap, Security, Spec §FR-011]
- [x] CHK014 Is the treatment of relative and protocol-relative link targets specified, since neither carries a scheme for the allowlist to match? [Gap, Security, Spec §FR-011]
- [x] CHK015 Are requirements stated for whitespace, control characters or encoded sequences embedded in a scheme before it is matched? [Gap, Security, Spec §FR-011]
- [x] CHK016 Is it specified that the allowlist is a comparison against a parsed scheme rather than a prefix or substring test? [Clarity, Security, Spec §FR-011]
- [x] CHK017 Are requirements stated for how a rendered external link opens, and what referrer or opener protections apply to it? [Gap, Security, Spec §FR-011]
- [x] CHK018 Is it specified that a link's visible text is escaped by the same rule as body text, so the text cannot carry markup the href is denied? [Gap, Security, Spec §FR-010, §FR-011]

## Escaping and Storage

- [x] CHK019 Is HTML escaping specified for every position — inside headings, list items, link text and inline code — rather than for the description as a whole? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK020 Is it stated that the subset constrains rendering only, and that source text outside the subset is stored verbatim rather than rejected on write? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010, §FR-039]
- [x] CHK021 Is the 10 000-character bound specified as applying to the markdown source rather than to the rendered output? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012, §FR-027]
- [x] CHK022 Are requirements stated for control characters, null bytes and bidirectional-override characters in a description? [Gap, Security, Spec §FR-010, §FR-012]
- [x] CHK023 Does FR-010's "structured elements rather than an HTML string" constraint belong in a specification that claims to carry no implementation details, or is it a plan-layer decision? [Scope, Spec §FR-010, §checklists/requirements.md]

## Render Surfaces and Consistency

- [x] CHK024 Is it specified whether Create project renders a description preview, given FR-039's render-on-read rule is stated only for the details screen? [Gap, Consistency, Spec §FR-027, §FR-039]
- [x] CHK025 Is it required that every surface rendering a description uses an identical grammar, so the second caller cannot diverge? [Gap, Consistency, Spec §FR-010, §Dependencies]
- [x] CHK026 Is the transition between rendered output and raw source specified for what the editor shows when a description is empty? [Gap, Edge Case, Spec §FR-039]
- [x] CHK027 Are requirements stated bounding the cost of rendering a maximum-length description with pathological nesting? [Gap, Non-Functional, Spec §FR-010, §FR-012]
- [x] CHK028 Is there a measurable success criterion covering the markdown subset, the escaping rule and the scheme allowlist, or do the Success Criteria omit this surface entirely? [Gap, Coverage, Traceability, Spec §Success Criteria]

## Resolution log

Recorded 2026-08-31 at the reviewer's request, after walking every item against
[`docs/product/specifications.md`](../../../docs/product/specifications.md),
[`docs/product/requirements-index.md`](../../../docs/product/requirements-index.md),
[`AGENTS.md`](../../../AGENTS.md) and this feature's own plan artifacts.

**Covered** — the requirement was already answered, in this spec or in a document it inherits from; the
citation is given and nothing changed. **Resolved** — the gap was real and a change was made; what
changed is named.

- **CHK001** · *Covered* — The contract's block table: "Paragraph | anything else", with source split on blank lines. Paragraphs are the fall-through, which is why FR-010 does not enumerate them.
- **CHK002** · *Covered* — The contract's inline table: bold is `**text**`, italic `*text*` or `_text_`. `__bold__` is not admitted — a decision, not an omission.
- **CHK003** · *Covered* — `#` … `######` → `h1` … `h6`. Where those levels sit relative to the screen's own headings is a rendering matter for project details, not a grammar one.
- **CHK004** · *Covered* — "Nesting is not supported. A list item is a line of inlines, never a list." Now extended: an indented line is a paragraph, since the block table has no indentation rule.
- **CHK005** · *Covered* — Inlines apply inside every block, and "Inline code wins" settles the overlap case explicitly — `` `**a**` `` renders five characters inside a `code` element.
- **CHK006** · *Resolved* — The contract now states ordinals are not honoured: a list written `3.` `4.` `5.` renders 1, 2, 3, because the subset has no node for a start offset.
- **CHK007** · *Resolved* — The contract now states there is no escape character, with the reason — admitting `\*` would mean deciding what a lone backslash does everywhere else.
- **CHK008** · *Covered* — "An unclosed marker is not a marker… There is no error state", and the contract now says so directly: the parser is total, so there is no parse failure for a screen to handle.
- **CHK009** · *Covered* — The contract enumerates the fall-through set: table row, blockquote, fenced code block, indented code block, image, embed, HTML tag — "no node type exists for them".
- **CHK010** · *Covered* — Fenced, indented and blockquote are named; a horizontal rule falls under "anything else" → paragraph, which is the identical treatment.
- **CHK011** · *Resolved* — The contract now states only `[text](href)` is a link: bare URLs, angle-bracket autolinks and reference-style `[text][id]` each render as their own text, so there is no scheme check to run on them.
- **CHK012** · *Covered* — Both cases are stated and the asymmetry is deliberate: an unsupported block "appears as its own literal text", while a link whose scheme fails renders "the link's text as plain text — not a dead anchor, and not the raw source".
- **CHK013** · *Covered* — The check parses the href with the `URL` constructor and compares `protocol`; `JaVaScRiPt:` is named as a bypass prefix-matching would let through.
- **CHK014** · *Resolved* — Relative hrefs were already covered; the contract now adds that a protocol-relative `//host/path` fails to parse without a base and lands in the same branch.
- **CHK015** · *Covered* — Leading whitespace and `java\nscript:` are named, and parsing rather than prefix-matching is precisely what handles them.
- **CHK016** · *Covered* — Stated in terms: "It does **not** match a prefix."
- **CHK017** · *Resolved* — The contract now specifies `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and same-tab opening, with the reasoning — a description is a record field, not a feed of outbound links.
- **CHK018** · *Covered* — The renderer returns React nodes, so escaping is structural: link text is a text node like any other, and there is no position at which it could be skipped.
- **CHK019** · *Covered* — Same mechanism — no markup is assembled anywhere, so there is no position-dependent escaping to get wrong.
- **CHK020** · *Covered* — "Stored as markdown source. The renderer runs on read." The subset constrains rendering; storage is verbatim, and nothing outside the subset is rejected on write.
- **CHK021** · *Covered* — §5 bounds the column and §3.7 stores the source in that column, so the bound is on the source by construction.
- **CHK022** · *Resolved* — The contract now states control and bidirectional-override characters are not stripped: they cannot close an element or open an attribute where no markup is assembled, and stripping would silently rewrite an author's text — which II forbids as surely as accepting bad input.
- **CHK023** · *In scope, judged* — FR-010 cites AGENTS.md's architecture note rather than choosing an implementation. The spec's own *Notes* already defends this pattern for `OT-DATA-001` and its neighbours: restating a decision taken upstream is traceability, not a technical choice made here.
- **CHK024** · *Resolved* — FR-027: the create form offers no rendered preview — the field holds source, and the rendered form is what project details shows on read.
- **CHK025** · *Covered* — FR-010 fixes the subset for the feature and *Dependencies* names R6 as the second call site, where Principle I decides promotion. One grammar, one module, two callers.
- **CHK026** · *Resolved* — The contract now specifies the empty case: a placeholder line opens the editor, carrying the same disabled reason for a non-member as every other field, and saving it empty is a legal write.
- **CHK027** · *Resolved* — Recorded as a default: at most 10 000 characters, a grammar with no nesting, rendered server-side for one field on one screen. No input in that space justifies a bound.
- **CHK028** · *Resolved* — SC-019 added, covering the subset, the literal-text fall-through and the scheme allowlist including schemes disguised by casing, leading whitespace or embedded control characters.

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
